title: $LONG^2RAG$: Evaluating Long-Context \& Long-Form Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Key Point Recall
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: Introduces Long2RAG benchmark and KPR metric for evaluating long-context and long-form RAG generation, including handling low signal-to-noise ratio in retrieved documents. Relevant for robust RAG evaluation.

title: A Hybrid Retrieval Approach for Advancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 7th International Conference on Natural Language and Speech Processing (ICNLSP 2024)
notes: Proposes a hybrid text+KG retrieval pipeline to improve retriever accuracy in a health-tech RAG use case. While it briefly mentions 'false retrieval', it does not analyze, benchmark, or mitigate retrieval noise/robustness in a principled way, nor address adversarial attacks, conflicts, calibration, answerability, or distraction. It is a general RAG improvement method rather than a robust-RAG contribution.

title: Accelerating Inference of Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Sparse Context Selection
authors: Yun Zhu; Jia-Chen Gu; Caitlin Sikora; Ho Ko; Yinxiao Liu; Chu-Cheng Lin; Lei Shu; Liangchen Luo; Lei Meng; Bang Liu; Jindong Chen
notes: Efficiency-focused sparse context selection for RAG; mentions robustness as side benefit but primary focus is latency, not robust RAG evaluation.

title: AceSearcher: Bootstrapping Reasoning and Search for LLMs via Reinforced Self-Play
authors: Ran Xu; Yuchen Zhuang; Zihan Dong; Ruiyu Wang; Yue Yu; Joyce C. Ho; Linjun Zhang; Haoyu Wang; Wenqi Shi; Carl Yang
notes: Generic multi-hop RAG capability paper using self-play RL for question decomposition and answer generation. Focuses on accuracy improvement on complex reasoning QA, not on robustness axes (noise, distraction, conflicts, attacks, calibration, answerability). No robust-RAG evaluation or mitigation.

title: Attention in Large Language Models Yields Efficient Zero-Shot Re-Rankers
authors: Shijie Chen; Bernal Jimenez Gutierrez; Yu Su
notes: Proposes in-context re-ranking using LLM attention weights for efficient zero-shot re-ranking. Focuses on retrieval/re-ranking efficiency and accuracy, not on robustness of RAG to noise, adversarial perturbations, or context failures. Background relevance only.

title: BSharedRAG: Backbone Shared Retrieval-Augmented Generation for the E-commerce Domain
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: Domain-specific e-commerce RAG method paper proposing a shared backbone with LoRA modules for retriever and generator. Focus is on domain adaptation and parameter sharing, not on robustness, noise, distraction, conflict, adversarial, or calibration analysis. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Boosting the Potential of Large Language Models with an Intelligent Information Assistant
authors: Yujia Zhou; Zheng Liu; Zhicheng Dou
notes: AssistRAG proposes an assistant LLM for memory and knowledge management to improve QA performance. While it includes a decision step on whether to use retrieved info, the focus is on boosting RAG capability rather than robustness, conflict, noise, or adversarial concerns. Background only.

title: BordIRlines: A Dataset for Evaluating Cross-lingual Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Advancing Natural Language Processing for Wikipedia
notes: Introduces BordIRlines, a cross-lingual RAG evaluation dataset focused on geopolitical disputes. Directly evaluates RAG robustness when context contains competing perspectives across languages, studying consistency/conflict in LLM responses. Fits evaluation_benchmark primary with knowledge_conflict secondary (multilingual sources with conflicting viewpoints) and multimodal_agentic_code as cross-lingual is a domain-specific setting.

title: C-3PO: Compact Plug-and-Play Proxy Optimization to Achieve Human-like Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors:
Guoxin Chen, Minpeng Liao, Peiying Yu, Dingmin Wang, Zile Qiao, Chao Yang, Xin Zhao, Kai Fan;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:8530-8551
notes: C-3PO proposes a proxy-centric multi-agent framework with agents that decide when to retrieve, filter retrieved information, and determine sufficiency for answering. Addresses adaptive retrieval control and noisy retrieval filtering, relevant to robust RAG.

title: Can Knowledge-Graph-based Retrieval Augmented Generation Really Retrieve What You Need?
authors: Junchi Yu; Yujie Liu; Jindong Gu; Philip Torr; Dongzhan Zhou
notes: Proposes GraphFlow for accurate/diverse KG-based RAG retrieval on complex queries. Focus is on retrieval quality/diversity for KGs, not on robust RAG axes like noise, distractors, conflict, adversarial corruption, or calibration. Mentions robustness only as generalization to unseen KGs. Out of scope.

title: Chunk-Distilled Language Modeling
authors: Yanhong Li; Karen Livescu; Jiawei Zhou
notes: CD-LM is a retrieval-augmented language modeling method focused on inference efficiency (multi-token chunk generation) and training-free domain adaptation via chunk distillation. While it uses retrieval, it does not address robustness concerns such as noisy retrieval, distraction, knowledge conflict, adversarial attacks, uncertainty/calibration, or answerability. No robust RAG evaluation or mechanism. Out of scope.

title: Context Tuning for Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Uncertainty-Aware NLP (UncertaiNLP 2024)
notes: Paper proposes context tuning to improve tool retrieval and plan generation in RAG. Addresses underspecified queries but framed as retrieval enhancement for tool use, not robustness to noise/attacks/conflicts. Mentions hallucination reduction tangentially. Closest to ood_uncertainty (implicit queries) but lacks explicit robustness analysis or evaluation under adversarial/noisy conditions. Boundary background.

title: Cooperative Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Question Answering: Mutual Information Exchange and Ranking by Contrasting Layers
authors: Youmin Ko; Sung Jong Seo; Hyunjoon Kim
notes: CoopRAG is a generic RAG framework improvement for multi-hop QA via query unrolling, contrasting-layer reranking, and reasoning chain completion. It does not explicitly study robustness to noise, distractors, conflicts, attacks, or uncertainty; evaluation is standard QA accuracy on HotpotQA/2Wiki/MuSiQue/NQ. No robust RAG angle.

title: Crafting Personalized Agents through Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Editable Memory Graphs
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: Application paper on personalized agents using editable memory graphs with RL-based adaptive memory selection. Mentions noise from irrelevant memories and adaptive selection but does not systematically study RAG robustness, attacks, or evaluation. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: DSLR: Document Refinement with Sentence-Level Re-ranking and Reconstruction to Enhance Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 3rd Workshop on Knowledge Augmented Methods for NLP
notes: DSLR proposes unsupervised sentence-level re-ranking and reconstruction to filter irrelevant/redundant info from retrieved passages, directly addressing noisy retrieval and LLM distraction in RAG. Workshop paper at ACL KnowledgeNLP 2024, evaluated on open-domain QA benchmarks. Fits robust RAG context-refinement mitigation.

title: EAReranker: Efficient Embedding Adequacy Assessment for Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Dongyang Zeng; Yaping Liu; Wei Zhang; Shuo Zhang; Xinwang Liu; Binxing Fang
notes: Embedding-based reranker focused on efficiency/privacy and adequacy scoring; only tangentially touches filtering inadequate documents, lacks explicit robustness evaluation.

title: Entity-Focused Dense Passage Retrieval for Outside-Knowledge Visual Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: Paper proposes Entity-Focused Dense Passage Retrieval for OK-VQA. It improves retrieval quality for multimodal QA but does not study robustness of RAG against noise, distractors, conflicts, adversarial attacks, or calibration. Out of scope for the robust RAG map.

title: FiD-Light: Efficient and Effective Retrieval-Augmented Text Generation
authors: Sebastian Hofstätter; Jiecao Chen; Karthik Raman; Hamed Zamani
notes: FiD-Light focuses on efficiency-effectiveness tradeoffs in retrieval-augmented generation, not on robustness aspects such as noisy retrieval, adversarial attack, knowledge conflict, or calibration. While it touches on robustness of source pointing distribution shift, this is a minor architectural choice rather than a robust RAG study. Background/foundational RAG work, not core evidence for the robust RAG map.

title: Graph-KV: Breaking Sequence via Injecting Structural Biases into Large Language Models
authors: Haoyu Peter Wang; Peihao Wang; Mufei Li; Shikun Liu; Siqi Miao; Zhangyang Wang; Pan Li
notes: Graph-KV addresses positional bias and serialization issues in RAG by structuring KV-cache attention via source-target relationships. Evaluated on 7 RAG benchmarks including multi-hop reasoning and long-document understanding. Directly tackles context utilization robustness.

title: Hierarchical Planning for Complex Tasks with Knowledge Graph-RAG and Symbolic Verification
authors:
Flavio Petruzzellis, Cristina Cornelio, Pietro Lio;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:49105-49127
notes: Paper proposes a neuro-symbolic hierarchical planning method (HVR) that integrates KG-based RAG and symbolic verification for robotic task planning. RAG is used as a knowledge source for planning, but the paper does not study retrieval robustness, noisy/adversarial retrieval, knowledge conflict, calibration, or evaluate RAG robustness specifically. Robustness here refers to plan correctness via symbolic validation, not RAG robustness. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Holistic Reasoning with Long-Context LMs: A Benchmark for Database Operations on Massive Textual Data
authors: Seiji Maekawa; Hayate Iso; Nikita Bhutani
notes: HoloBench benchmarks long-context LMs vs RAG on holistic reasoning over large textual data, varying context length, info density, position, and query complexity. Relevant to RAG evaluation and long-context distraction analysis, though framed as LCLM benchmark contrasted with RAG.

title: HyPA-RAG: A Hybrid Parameter Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for AI Legal and Policy Applications
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Customizable NLP: Progress and Challenges in Customizing NLP for a Domain, Application, Group, or Individual (CustomNLP4U)
notes: Domain RAG system with adaptive parameter selection, hybrid retrieval, and custom evaluation framework targeting common RAG failure points in legal/policy QA.

title: Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yiqun Chen; Lingyong Yan; Weiwei Sun; Xinyu Ma; Yi Zhang; Shuaiqiang Wang; Dawei Yin; Yiming Yang; Jiaxin Mao
notes: Paper proposes MMOA-RAG, a multi-agent RL framework to jointly optimize query rewriter, retriever, selector, and generator modules in a RAG pipeline. Focus is on end-to-end optimization for answer F1, not on robustness aspects (noise, distraction, conflict, adversarial, calibration). No explicit robust RAG angle, so out of scope.

title: KnowGPT: Knowledge Graph based Prompting for Large Language Models
authors: Qinggang Zhang; Junnan Dong; Hao Chen; Daochen Zha; Zailiang Yu; Xiao Huang
notes: KnowGPT is a KG-based prompting framework using RL and MAB for knowledge extraction and prompt construction. Focus is on effectiveness and cost of GraphRAG for QA, not on robustness analysis (no explicit study of noise, conflicts, adversarial corruption, or calibration). Background/boundary for robust RAG map.

title: Knowledge-Consistent Dialogue Generation with Knowledge Graphs
authors: Minki Kang; Jin Myung Kwak; Jinheon Baek; Sung Ju Hwang
notes: SURGE proposes subgraph retrieval-augmented dialogue generation with KG, addressing irrelevant knowledge and hallucination via contrastive learning. While related to faithfulness and noisy retrieval, focus is on KG-grounded dialogue generation rather than robust RAG evaluation or attack/defense. Background relevance only.

title: Knowledge-Consistent Dialogue Generation with Language Models and Knowledge Graphs
authors: Minki Kang; Jin Myung Kwak; Jinheon Baek; Sung Ju Hwang
notes: SURGE is a KG-augmented dialogue generation method that retrieves relevant subgraphs and uses contrastive learning to enforce knowledge consistency. While it touches on filtering irrelevant facts and reducing hallucination, it predates the LLM-RAG robustness literature and does not explicitly study robust RAG attacks, defenses, or systematic robustness evaluation. Background only.

title: LI-RAGE: Late Interaction Retrieval Augmented Generation with Explicit Signals for Open-Domain Table Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 2: Short Papers)
notes: Paper proposes LI-RAGE for open-domain TableQA with late interaction retrieval and binary relevance token. Focus is on improving SOTA accuracy, not robustness to noise, attacks, or conflicts. Not a robust RAG contribution.

title: LLM-Check: Investigating Detection of Hallucinations in Large Language Models
authors: Gaurang Sriramanan; Siddhant Bharti; Vinu Sankar Sadasivan; Shoumik Saha; Priyatham Kattakinda; Soheil Feizi
notes: LLM-Check proposes hallucination detection using internal attention/hidden states/probabilities; explicitly includes RAG setting with RAGTruth dataset. Relevant to robust RAG via hallucination/faithfulness detection, though RAG is only one of several evaluation settings.

title: LLMs as Collaborator: Demands-Guided Collaborative Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Commonsense Knowledge-Grounded Open-Domain Dialogue Systems
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: Generic RAG method paper for commonsense knowledge-grounded open-domain dialogue. Proposes DCRAG using LLMs as collaborators to retrieve from knowledge graphs. No explicit robustness angle: no analysis of retrieval noise, no adversarial attacks, no knowledge conflicts, no calibration/abstention. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Lift Yourself Up: Retrieval-augmented Text Generation with Self-Memory
authors: Xin Cheng; Di Luo; Xiuying Chen; Lemao Liu; Dongyan Zhao; Rui Yan
notes: Generic RAG improvement method using self-generated memory iteratively. Focuses on text generation quality (MT, summarization, dialogue) without any robustness angle - no analysis of noisy retrieval, distraction, conflicts, attacks, calibration, or answerability. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: M-RAG: Reinforcing Large Language Model Performance through Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Multiple Partitions
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: M-RAG proposes a multi-partition RAG framework with multi-agent RL to improve generation quality on summarization, translation, and dialogue tasks. While it briefly mentions noise from coarse-grained retrieval, the paper focuses on performance improvement rather than robustness analysis, attack/defense, calibration, or evaluation of robust RAG axes. Not a robust RAG contribution.

title: Modeling Uncertainty and Using Post-fusion as Fallback Improves Retrieval Augmented Generation with LLMs
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Towards Knowledgeable Language Models (KnowLLM 2024)
notes: Paper investigates uncertainty modeling (LLM 'unknown' outputs) and proposes post-fusion fallback and concatenation-as-distiller strategies to improve RAG when retrieved passages contain the answer but the model fails. Addresses calibration/control (when to fall back) and distraction from retrieved passages. Tested on NQ, TriviaQA, SQuAD. Directly relevant to robust RAG.

title: Multi-Hop Paragraph Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
notes: Paper proposes MUPPET, an iterative multi-hop paragraph retrieval method for open-domain QA (SQuAD-Open, HotpotQA). It is a retrieval/QA architecture contribution, not a study of robustness, noise, distraction, conflict, adversarial perturbation, calibration, or answerability. While multi-hop retrieval is foundational background for downstream RAG robustness work, it does not explicitly analyze, benchmark, attack, or mitigate retrieval/context robustness. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Multi-Level Information Retrieval Augmented Generation for Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: Multi-level entity+passage RAG for KB-VQA. Mentions noisy pseudo-relevance and irrelevant passage issues, but focus is on improving accuracy via multi-level retrieval, not robustness analysis or defenses. Boundary multimodal RAG work.

title: Multi-Task Dense Retrieval via Model Uncertainty Fusion for Open-Domain Question Answering
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2021
notes: Paper proposes multi-task dense retrieval via ensemble model uncertainty fusion across DPR experts for open-domain QA. Uncertainty estimation is used as a dynamic weighting scheme for expert selection, not for RAG calibration, abstention, or robustness against noisy/adversarial/conflicting retrieval. No RAG generator-side analysis, no robustness threat model. Generic dense retrieval contribution; out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Neural Graph Matching Improves Retrieval Augmented Generation in Molecular Machine Learning
authors:
Runzhong Wang, Rui-Xi Wang, Mrunali Manjrekar, Connor W. Coley;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:64734-64749
notes: Domain-specific RAG for molecular machine learning (mass spectrum simulation) using neural graph matching. While it mentions noise-robust matching, robustness pertains to structural ambiguity in retrieved molecules for GNNs, not LLM-based RAG robustness. Not about retrieval noise, distraction, conflicts, attacks, or calibration in LLM RAG.

title: NutriBench: A Dataset for Evaluating Large Language Models in Nutrition Estimation from Meal Descriptions
authors: Mehak Preet Dhaliwal; Andong Hua; Laya Pullela; Ryan Burke; Yao Qin
notes: Domain-specific (nutrition) benchmark that evaluates LLMs with standard, CoT, and RAG prompting on carbohydrate estimation. RAG is used only as one prompting strategy; no robustness analysis (no noise, distraction, conflict, adversarial, calibration, or answerability angle) for RAG. Out of scope for the robust RAG map.

title: Online Adaptation of Language Models with a Memory of Amortized Contexts
authors: Jihoon Tack; Jaehyung Kim; Eric Mitchell; Jinwoo Shin; Yee Whye Teh; Jonathan Richard Schwarz
notes: Paper proposes Memory of Amortized Contexts (MAC), an online adaptation framework for LLMs using PEFT modulations and amortization-based meta-learning. While it briefly mentions RAG as a complementary method and notes counterfactual sensitivity, the core contribution is about efficient online finetuning/adaptation, not robust RAG mechanisms. No explicit analysis of retrieval noise, distraction, conflict, or adversarial robustness.

title: Optimizing Retrieval for RAG via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Jiawei Zhou; Lei Chen
notes: Paper proposes R3, an RL-based retrieval optimization framework for RAG. While it mentions retrieval gaps (semantically related but unhelpful content, misleading evidence), the focus is on improving RAG retrieval performance via RL rather than robustness to noise, adversarial attacks, or conflicts. Not directly a robust RAG paper; closest category is noisy retrieval as background.

title: Patent Response System Optimised for Faithfulness: Procedural Knowledge Embodiment with Knowledge Graph and Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Towards Knowledgeable Language Models (KnowLLM 2024)
notes: Domain-specific patent response system using RAG and KG. Focuses on faithfulness in patent domain, not on robust RAG mechanisms broadly applicable. No analysis of retrieval noise, conflicts, attacks, or calibration. Out of scope.

title: PlanRAG: A Plan-then-Retrieval Augmented Generation for Generative Large Language Models as Decision Makers
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: PlanRAG proposes an iterative plan-then-retrieve RAG technique for decision-making QA over structured databases with a new DQA benchmark. Focus is on planning capability for complex decisions, not on robustness against noise, distraction, conflict, attacks, or calibration. Not a robust RAG contribution.

title: Quebec Automobile Insurance Question-Answering With Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the Natural Legal Language Processing Workshop 2024
notes: Domain-specific application of RAG for Quebec automobile insurance QA. Introduces corpora and evaluates GPT-4o, but does not focus on robustness, noise, attacks, calibration, or systematic robust RAG analysis. Background/application paper without robust RAG angle.

title: R$^2$AG: Incorporating Retrieval Information into Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: R2AG bridges the semantic gap between retrievers and LLMs via a R2-Former and retrieval-aware prompting. Explicitly addresses noisy/low-quality retrieved documents and lost-in-middle issues; claims robustness in experiments. Primary angle is mitigation of retrieval noise via context assembly, with distraction as secondary. EMNLP Findings 2024.

title: RAG-HAT: A Hallucination-Aware Tuning Pipeline for LLM in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: Industry Track
notes: RAG-HAT proposes hallucination-aware fine-tuning pipeline with detection and DPO-based mitigation for RAG outputs, directly addressing faithfulness/context-grounding robustness in RAG.

title: RAG-SR: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Neural Symbolic Regression
authors: Hengzhe Zhang; Qi Chen; Bing XUE; Wolfgang Banzhaf; Mengjie Zhang
notes: Applies a retrieval-augmented generation mechanism to neural symbolic regression to reduce hallucinations in generated symbolic trees. Not about robustness of RAG for LLM QA/text retrieval; uses RAG only as a domain technique in symbolic regression.

title: RAG-Studio: Towards In-Domain Adaptation of Retrieval Augmented Generation Through Self-Alignment
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: Self-aligned domain adaptation framework jointly fine-tuning retriever and generator; touches noisy context handling via helpful/irrelevant/misleading classification but primary focus is domain adaptation, not robustness.

title: RAG4GFM: Bridging Knowledge Gaps in Graph Foundation Models through Graph Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Xingliang Wang; Zemin Liu; Junxiao Han; Shuiguang Deng
notes: Paper proposes RAG4GFM, a graph-RAG framework for Graph Foundation Models with multi-level graph indexing, task-aware retrieval, and graph fusion. Focus is knowledge updating and reasoning fidelity for GFMs, not robust RAG concerns. No analysis of retrieval noise, distractors, conflicts, attacks, or abstention. Out of scope.

title: RAGLAB: A Modular and Research-Oriented Unified Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: System Demonstrations
notes: RAGLAB is a generic modular RAG framework for fair comparison of 6 RAG algorithms across 10 benchmarks. It is a general-purpose research toolkit/library without specific focus on robustness, adversarial settings, noise, distractors, or knowledge conflicts. Useful as background/positioning for RAG evaluation infrastructure but not direct evidence for robust RAG.

title: RAGRouter: Learning to Route Queries to Multiple Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Jiarui Zhang; Xiangyu Liu; Yong Hu; Chaoyue Niu; Fan Wu; Guihai Chen
notes: RAGRouter learns to route queries across multiple retrieval-augmented LLMs based on their differing RAG capabilities. While it touches on heterogeneous robustness to retrieval noise, the core contribution is model selection/routing rather than robustness analysis, mitigation, or evaluation of retrieval failures. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: RAGViz: Diagnose and Visualize Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: System Demonstrations
notes: RAGViz visualizes attention on retrieved docs to diagnose hallucinations from parametric vs retrieved sources, supporting context utilization analysis.

title: RAPID: Long-Context Inference with Retrieval-Augmented Speculative Decoding
authors:
Guanzheng Chen, Qilong Feng, Jinjie Ni, Xin Li, Michael Qizhe Shieh;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:8093-8107
notes: RAPID is an inference acceleration method combining RAG with speculative decoding for long-context LLMs. Focus is efficiency/throughput, not robustness. Brief robustness-to-retrieval-quality analysis is incidental, not a robust RAG contribution.

title: ReFIR: Grounding Large Restoration Models with Retrieval Augmentation
authors: Hang Guo; Tao Dai; Zhihao Ouyang; Taolin Zhang; Yaohua Zha; Bin Chen; Shu-Tao Xia
notes: Image restoration with retrieved reference images; uses RAG analogy but applied to vision, not LLM RAG robustness. Out of scope.

title: ReMindRAG: Low-Cost LLM-Guided Knowledge Graph Traversal for Efficient RAG
authors: Yikuan Hu; Jifeng Zhu; Lanrui Tang; Chen Huang
notes: Proposes KG-RAG system with LLM-guided graph traversal and memory replay for cost-effective multi-hop retrieval. Focus is on effectiveness/efficiency trade-off, not robustness to noise, attacks, conflicts, or uncertainty. No explicit robust RAG angle.

title: RealRAG: Retrieval-augmented Realistic Image Generation via Self-reflective Contrastive Learning
authors:
Yuanhuiyi Lyu, Xu Zheng, Lutao Jiang, Yibo Yan, Xin Zou, Huiyu Zhou, Linfeng Zhang, Xuming Hu;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:41772-41790
notes: RealRAG is a retrieval-augmented framework for text-to-image generation that uses a reflective retriever to improve realism for fine-grained/novel object generation. While it is multimodal RAG, the focus is on generation quality and bridging knowledge gaps in image generators, not on robustness aspects like noisy retrieval analysis, adversarial corruption, knowledge conflicts, or calibration. It does not study or evaluate robustness of RAG in any of the taxonomy senses, so it is out of scope for

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Rich Answer Encoding
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 13th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing and the 3rd Conference of the Asia-Pacific Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: Paper proposes new training objectives (DKS, RAC) to improve retriever generalization in RAG by addressing false-negative passage problem. Robustness mentioned is about training generalization, not handling noisy/adversarial context or evaluating robustness axes. Not core robust RAG.

title: Retrieval augmented text-to-SQL generation for epidemiological question answering using electronic health records
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 6th Clinical Natural Language Processing Workshop
notes: Domain-specific RAG application for text-to-SQL on EHR/claims data. Uses RAG to improve SQL generation but does not study robustness, noise, distraction, conflicts, attacks, or calibration. No robust RAG angle.

title: Retrieval-augmented Generation across Heterogeneous Knowledge
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies: Student Research Workshop
notes: Thesis proposal at NAACL SRW surveying RAG and proposing extensions to heterogeneous knowledge sources (text, tables, KGs). Briefly notes that scaling to CCNet hurts NQ/HotpotQA performance, but the focus is improving coverage/knowledge integration, not robustness, noise mitigation, conflict handling, calibration, or attacks. Background only; not direct evidence for the robust RAG map.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation in multilingual settings
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Towards Knowledgeable Language Models (KnowLLM 2024)
notes: Studies mRAG pipeline across 13 languages, evaluating retrieval and generation robustness in multilingual settings; identifies limitations like irrelevant retrieval, code-switching, and metric adjustments. Relevant as evaluation/benchmarking work for RAG robustness in cross-lingual setting.

title: Robust Retrieval Augmented Generation for Zero-shot Slot Filling
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: Paper uses robust in title but the robustness refers mainly to domain adaptation (zero/few-shot transfer to new TACRED variant) and hard negative mining for DPR in slot filling, not to noise/adversarial/conflict robustness central to robust RAG taxonomy. Application of RAG with retrieval improvements rather than a study of RAG failure modes.

title: SeRTS: Self-Rewarding Tree Search for Biomedical Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: Biomedical RAG method using MCTS and self-rewarding tree search to improve retrieval quality. Focuses on performance enhancement, not robustness analysis, noise/distraction/conflict, adversarial defense, or calibration. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Self-Retrieval: End-to-End Information Retrieval with One Large Language Model
authors: Qiaoyu Tang; Jiawei Chen; Zhuoqun Li; Bowen Yu; Yaojie Lu; ChengFu; Haiyang Yu; Hongyu Lin; Fei Huang; Ben He; Xianpei Han; Le Sun; Yongbin Li
notes: Paper proposes Self-Retrieval, an end-to-end generative IR architecture using one LLM for indexing, retrieval, and reranking. While RAG is mentioned as a downstream beneficiary, the paper does not study robustness aspects (noise, distraction, conflict, attacks, uncertainty, calibration). It is generic retrieval methodology, out of scope for the robust RAG map.

title: Superposition Prompting: Improving and Accelerating Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors:
Thomas Merth, Qichen Fu, Mohammad Rastegari, Mahyar Najibi;
    Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235:35507-35527
notes: ICML 2024 paper targeting the distraction phenomenon in RAG where irrelevant context degrades output. Proposes superposition prompting with path pruning to discard irrelevant documents, improving robustness and efficiency on QA benchmarks.

title: TRACE: Grounding Time Series in Context for Multimodal Embedding and Retrieval
authors: Jialin Chen; Ziyu Zhao; Gaukhar Nurbek; Aosong Feng; Ali Maatouk; Leandros Tassiulas; Yifeng Gao; Rex Ying
notes: TRACE is a cross-modal time-series/text retriever for time-series foundation models with RAG. Focus is on building a domain-specific multimodal retriever and embeddings for forecasting/classification, not on robustness analysis. No study of noise, distractors, conflicts, adversarial attacks, calibration, or answerability. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Towards Cross-Cultural Machine Translation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation from Multilingual Knowledge Graphs
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: Domain-specific RAG application for cross-cultural machine translation using multilingual knowledge graphs. Introduces XC-Translate benchmark and KG-MT method, but focus is on translation quality of cultural entity names, not RAG robustness. No analysis of retrieval noise, distraction, conflicts, or attacks.

title: Two-tiered Encoder-based Hallucination Detection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in the Wild
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: Industry Track
notes: Proposes RAGHalu, a two-tiered encoder-based hallucination/faithfulness detector for enterprise RAG. Directly addresses ungrounded responses (knowledge conflict between LLM output and KB) and supports abstain/escalation control; introduces re-annotated datasets. Relevant as supporting evidence for robust RAG faithfulness detection.

title: Unified Generative and Discriminative Training for Multi-modal Large Language Models
authors: Wei Chow; Juncheng Li; Qifan Yu; Kaihang Pan; Hao Fei; Zhiqi Ge; Shuai Yang; Siliang Tang; Hanwang Zhang; Qianru Sun
notes: Paper focuses on unifying generative and discriminative training paradigms for multimodal LLMs. While it mentions using RAG as a downstream strategy to enhance generative task performance, the primary contribution is on training methodology (Dynamic Time Warping, structure-induced constraints), not on robustness, evaluation, attacks, defenses, or calibration of RAG systems. No specific robust RAG angle.

title: WebBrain: Learning to Generate Factually Correct Articles for Queries by Grounding on Large Web Corpus
authors: Hongjin Qian; Yutao Zhu; Zhicheng Dou; Haoqi Gu; Xinyu Zhang; Zheng Liu; Ruofei Lai; Zhao Cao; Jian-Yun Nie; Ji-Rong Wen
notes: WebBrain introduces a dataset and ReGen framework for generating factual Wikipedia-style articles grounded on web evidence. While related to retrieval-augmented generation and factuality, it focuses on a new generation task rather than robustness analysis (no explicit study of noisy/adversarial retrieval, conflicts, calibration, or robustness perturbations). Background only.

title: Chain of Agents: Large Language Models Collaborating on Long-Context Tasks
authors: Yusen Zhang; Ruoxi Sun; Yanfei Chen; Tomas Pfister; Rui Zhang; Sercan O Arik
notes: Proposes Chain-of-Agents multi-agent framework for long-context tasks. RAG appears only as a comparison baseline; the paper is about long-context processing alternatives, not about robust RAG mechanisms, retrieval noise, or RAG evaluation. Touches lost-in-the-middle issue but not as a robust RAG contribution. Out of scope.

title: ChatQA 2: Bridging the Gap to Proprietary LLMs in Long Context and RAG Capabilities
authors: Peng Xu; Wei Ping; Xianchao Wu; Chejian Xu; Zihan Liu; Mohammad Shoeybi; Bryan Catanzaro
notes: ChatQA 2 builds a long-context plus RAG capable open model and evaluates on ChatRAGBench. Touches RAG robustness via chunk-size variation and top-k retrieval trade-offs (irrelevant context with large k), and explicitly compares long-context vs RAG. Primarily a capability/evaluation paper rather than a robustness-focused study, so support-level.

title: ChatQA: Surpassing GPT-4 on Conversational QA and RAG
authors: Zihan Liu; Wei Ping; Rajarshi Roy; Peng Xu; Chankyu Lee; Mohammad Shoeybi; Bryan Catanzaro
notes: ChatQA introduces ChatRAG Bench including unanswerable scenarios and conversational RAG evaluation; relevant to RAG benchmarking and answerability/abstention, though primary contribution is instruction tuning recipe for RAG/conversational QA.

title: Deliberation on Priors: Trustworthy Reasoning of Large Language Models on Knowledge Graphs
authors: Jie Ma; Ning Qu; Zhitao Gao; Xing Rui; Jun Liu; Hongbin Pei; Jiang Xie; Lingyun Song; Pinghui Wang; Jing Tao; su zhou
notes: KG-RAG method using priors and introspection for faithful reasoning; not focused on robustness to noise, conflicts, or attacks.

title: Do Metadata and Appearance of the Retrieved Webpages Affect LLM's Reasoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation?
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 7th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
notes: Studies how non-textual metadata (publication time, source, visual appearance) of retrieved webpages affects LLM reasoning when documents present conflicting evidence in RAG. Directly addresses knowledge conflict and source preference in RAG; also introduces ConflictingQA-Fake dataset. BlackboxNLP workshop venue, useful supporting evidence for robust RAG map.

title: Optimizing LLM Based Retrieval Augmented Generation Pipelines in the Financial Domain
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 6: Industry Track)
notes: Empirical study benchmarks 6 LLMs across 15 retrieval conditions and 9 prompts on two financial RAG datasets. Probes robustness to missing gold docs, distractor count, and document ordering, plus prompt sensitivity. Relevant as evaluation/analysis evidence for retrieval-noise and distraction robustness in RAG.

title: Position: Retrieval-augmented systems can be dangerous medical communicators
authors:
Lionel Wong, Ayman Ali, Raymond M Xiong, Zejiang Shen, Yoon Kim, Monica Agrawal;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:82347-82359
notes: ICML position paper analyzing pragmatic misalignment in medical RAG; decontextualization and selective context cause misleading outputs despite literal accuracy

title: Reasoning-Enhanced Healthcare Predictions with Knowledge Graph Community Retrieval
authors: Pengcheng Jiang; Cao Xiao; Minhao Jiang; Parminder Bhatia; Taha Kass-Hout; Jimeng Sun; Jiawei Han
notes: Domain-specific KG-enhanced RAG for healthcare prediction (mortality/readmission on MIMIC). Focuses on improving prediction accuracy via KG community retrieval, not on robustness, noise analysis, adversarial attacks, conflicts, calibration, or RAG evaluation/benchmarking. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Reducing hallucination in structured outputs via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 6: Industry Track)
notes: Industry application paper using RAG to reduce hallucination in JSON workflow generation. Mentions OOD generalization and hallucination reduction, but it is primarily an applied system description, not a robustness study/benchmark/attack-defense. No analysis of retrieval noise, conflicts, distractors, or calibration mechanisms specific to robust RAG. Boundary/background only.

title: SV-RAG: LoRA-Contextualizing Adaptation of  MLLMs for Long Document Understanding
authors: Jian Chen; Ruiyi Zhang; Yufan Zhou; Tong Yu; Franck Dernoncourt; Jiuxiang Gu; Ryan A. Rossi; Changyou Chen; Tong Sun
notes: SV-RAG is a multimodal RAG framework using LoRA-adapted MLLMs for long visually-rich document understanding. Focus is on efficiency and accuracy, not robustness, noise, conflict, or adversarial issues. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: SearchLVLMs: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Augmenting Large Vision-Language Models by Searching Up-to-Date Internet Knowledge
authors: Chuanhao Li; Zhen Li; Chenchen Jing; Shuo Liu; Wenqi Shao; Yuwei Wu; Ping Luo; Yu Qiao; Kaipeng Zhang
notes: Multimodal internet-augmented generation framework with hierarchical filtering and UDK-VQA benchmark; addresses up-to-date knowledge for LVLMs but not explicitly a robustness study.

title: Vgent: Graph-based Retrieval-Reasoning-Augmented Generation For Long Video Understanding
authors: Xiaoqian Shen; Wenxuan Zhang; Jun Chen; Mohamed Elhoseiny
notes: Vgent proposes a graph-based RAG framework for long video understanding. While it touches on retrieval noise and distraction from irrelevant clips, the focus is on improving video QA accuracy via graph structure and structured reasoning, not on systematic robustness analysis, attack/defense, or calibration in RAG. Best treated as adjacent multimodal RAG background, not core robust RAG evidence.

title: VimoRAG: Video-based Retrieval-augmented 3D Motion Generation for Motion Language Models
authors: Haidong Xu; Guangwei Xu; Zhedong Zheng; Xiatian Zhu; Wei Ji; Xiangtai Li; Ruijie Guo; Meishan Zhang; Min zhang; Hao Fei
notes: Domain-specific video-based RAG for 3D motion generation. While it addresses error propagation from noisy retrieval, it is not about robust RAG for LLM text/QA systems and falls outside the map scope.

title: Visual Haystacks: A Vision-Centric Needle-In-A-Haystack Benchmark
authors: Tsung-Han Wu; Giscard Biamby; Jerome Quenum; Ritwik Gupta; Joseph E. Gonzalez; Trevor Darrell; David Chan
notes: Introduces Visual Haystacks benchmark for multi-image RAG, evaluates visual distractors and positional bias (lost-in-the-middle), and proposes MIRAGE visual-RAG framework. Relevant as multimodal robust RAG benchmark.

title: A Theory for Token-Level Harmonization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Shicheng Xu; Liang Pang; Huawei Shen; Xueqi Cheng
notes: ICLR 2025 paper provides theoretical framework for token-level trade-off between benefit and detriment in RAG, addressing noisy retrieval and knowledge conflict via Tok-RAG collaborative generation between pure LLM and RAG.

title: ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: ARES is a widely-cited NAACL 2024 automated evaluation framework for RAG systems, scoring context relevance, answer faithfulness, and answer relevance with PPI-based confidence intervals. Core evaluation/benchmark contribution directly relevant to robust RAG assessment.

title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: FLARE proposes active retrieval that decides when (low-probability tokens trigger retrieval) and what to retrieve (anticipated next sentence as query) during long-form generation. This is a canonical adaptive/calibrated retrieval control method, directly relevant to robust RAG. Evaluated on multihop QA, commonsense reasoning, long-form QA, and open-domain summarization. EMNLP 2023 main conference.

title: An Information Bottleneck Perspective for Effective Noise Filtering on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: ACL 2024 long paper introducing an information bottleneck-based noise filter for RAG. Directly targets noisy/irrelevant retrieved passages, proposes SFT and RL training objectives, and evaluates on NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA. Core robust RAG contribution addressing noisy retrieval and context distraction via context-assembly filtering.

title: Auto-GDA: Automatic Domain Adaptation for Efficient Grounding Verification in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Tobias Leemann; Periklis Petridis; Giuseppe Vietri; Dionysis Manousakas; Aaron Roth; Sergul Aydore
notes: ICLR 2025 paper on Auto-GDA, domain adaptation framework for lightweight NLI-based grounding verification in RAG. Addresses faithfulness verification of LLM output against retrieved evidence, directly relevant to robust RAG hallucination detection and control.

title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
notes: BEIR is a heterogeneous zero-shot IR benchmark explicitly targeting OOD generalization across 18 datasets and 9 tasks. Widely used as a retrieval robustness/OOD evaluation resource underpinning RAG retriever evaluation.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation with Dynamic VQA Dataset and Self-adaptive Planning Agent
authors: Yangning Li; Yinghui Li; Xinyu Wang; Yong Jiang; Zhen Zhang; Xinran Zheng; Hui Wang; Hai-Tao Zheng; Fei Huang; Jingren Zhou; Philip S. Yu
notes: Introduces Dyn-VQA benchmark for multimodal RAG with dynamic, multi-hop and time-varying questions, plus a self-adaptive planning agent (OmniSearch). Relevant as multimodal RAG benchmark and adaptive retrieval control.

title: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024
notes: MIRAGE benchmark systematically evaluates RAG components (corpora, retrievers, LLMs) for medical QA, including analysis of lost-in-the-middle effects and scaling. Provides domain-specific RAG evaluation resource relevant to robust RAG.

title: Boosting Knowledge Utilization in Multimodal Large Language Models via Adaptive Logits Fusion and Attention Reallocation
authors: Wenbin An; Jiahao Nie; Feng Tian; Haonan Lin; mingxiang cai; Yaqiang Wu; QianYing Wang; Xiaoqin Zhang; Shijian Lu
notes: ALFAR explicitly tackles knowledge conflicts between parametric and contextual knowledge in MRAG, plus attention bias (distraction-like) on retrieved context. Training-free generator-side intervention (logits fusion + attention reallocation) directly relevant to robust RAG. Multimodal setting is secondary.

title: Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Liang Wang; Haonan Chen; Nan Yang; Xiaolong Huang; Zhicheng Dou; Furu Wei
notes: CoRAG trains LLMs to iteratively retrieve and reformulate queries to handle imperfect retrieval, with claimed robustness against retrievers of varying quality. Adaptive retrieval control relevant to robust RAG.

title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
authors: Manuel Faysse; Hugues Sibille; Tony Wu; Bilel Omrani; Gautier Viaud; CELINE HUDELOT; Pierre Colombo
notes: ColPali introduces a vision-language document retrieval model and ViDoRe benchmark. It motivates RAG pipelines but does not address robustness, noise, adversarial attacks, conflicts, or calibration. Background only for visual RAG retrieval.

title: DRAGIN: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Real-time Information Needs of Large Language Models
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: DRAGIN proposes dynamic RAG deciding when and what to retrieve via real-time information needs detection and self-attention query formulation; addresses calibrated retrieval activation to avoid noisy unnecessary retrieval. ACL 2024 long paper, core evidence for adaptive retrieval control in robust RAG.

title: DeepDiver: Adaptive Web-Search Intensity Scaling via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Wenxuan Shi; Haochen Tan; Chuqiao Kuang; Xiaoguang Li; Hanting Chen; Xiaozhe Ren; Yasheng Wang; Lu Hou; Lifeng Shang
notes: DeepDiver uses RL to adaptively scale search frequency/depth in iterative RAG over noisy real-web sources, explicitly targeting conflict resolution, verification/denoising, and reflection. WebPuzzle benchmark also evaluates robustness in real-web settings. Fits calibration_control with noisy_retrieval and conflict aspects.

title: Do You Know What You Are Talking About? Characterizing Query-Knowledge Relevance For Reliable Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: EMNLP 2024 paper presenting a statistical goodness-of-fit framework for detecting out-of-knowledge queries online and query distribution shift offline in RAG, directly addressing answerability and reliable retrieval.

title: Follow My Instruction and Spill the Beans: Scalable Data Extraction from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Zhenting Qi; Hanlin Zhang; Eric P. Xing; Sham M. Kakade; Himabindu Lakkaraju
notes: ICLR 2025 paper that introduces a prompt-injection-based data extraction attack on Retrieval-In-Context RAG systems, evaluates vulnerability across many instruction-tuned LMs and production GPTs, and proposes position-bias-elimination defenses. Directly relevant to adversarial robustness of RAG.

title: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for Large Language Models
authors:
Bernal Jiménez Gutiérrez, Yiheng Shu, Weijian Qi, Sizhe Zhou, Yu Su;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:21497-21515
notes: HippoRAG 2 is a RAG architecture paper using KG + Personalized PageRank for continual learning. While it mentions 'robustness' across factual/sense-making/associative memory tasks, it does not address robust RAG failure modes from the taxonomy (noise, distractors, conflicts, adversarial, OOD, calibration). It is a RAG method paper, not a robust RAG study.

title: G-Retriever: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Textual Graph Understanding and Question Answering
authors: Xiaoxin He; Yijun Tian; Yifei Sun; Nitesh V Chawla; Thomas Laurent; Yann LeCun; Xavier Bresson; Bryan Hooi
notes: Introduces RAG approach for textual graph QA with GraphQA benchmark; mentions hallucination mitigation but primary focus is enabling graph QA, not robust RAG.

title: GFM-RAG: Graph Foundation Model for Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Linhao Luo; Zicheng Zhao; Gholamreza Haffari; Dinh Phung; Chen Gong; Shirui Pan
notes: GFM-RAG proposes a graph foundation model for RAG retrieval. While it briefly mentions noise/incompleteness in graph structure, the primary contribution is methodological (GFM-based retriever for multi-hop QA), not a robustness study/evaluation/attack/defense. Out of scope for robust RAG map; closest taxonomy bucket is noisy_retrieval, but inclusion rule requires explicit analysis/mitigation of retrieval noise, which is not the central contribution.

title: Generate-then-Ground in Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multi-hop Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: ACL 2024 paper proposing a generate-then-ground framework for multi-hop QA that explicitly mitigates retrieval noise and reconciles parametric vs. retrieved knowledge, fitting noisy_retrieval with a knowledge_conflict secondary angle.

title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
authors: Bernal Jimenez Gutierrez; Yiheng Shu; Yu Gu; Michihiro Yasunaga; Yu Su
notes: HippoRAG proposes a neurobiologically inspired RAG framework using knowledge graphs and Personalized PageRank for multi-hop QA. Focus is on knowledge integration and retrieval effectiveness, not on robustness aspects like noise, adversarial attacks, conflicts, or calibration. Not directly in scope for robust RAG map.

title: Influence Guided Context Selection for Effective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jiale Deng; Yanyan Shen; Ziyuan Pei; Youmin Chen; Linpeng Huang
notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper proposing Contextual Influence (CI) value and a surrogate model (CSM) for selecting high-quality contexts in RAG, explicitly addressing noise robustness against irrelevant/noisy retrieval results. Has a dedicated 'Noise Robustness for RAG' related work section, discusses distraction, lost-in-the-middle, and over-trust of contexts. Filters context list adaptively (calibration aspect via positive CI value threshold). Evaluated on 8 NLP tasks with 2 LLMs.

title: InstructRAG: Instructing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Self-Synthesized Rationales
authors: Zhepei Wei; Wei-Lin Chen; Yu Meng
notes: ICLR 2025 paper directly tackling noisy retrieval in RAG via self-synthesized denoising rationales used for ICL or SFT. Addresses imperfect retrievers/noisy corpora and shows robustness with increasing retrieved documents and OOD generalization. Clear core evidence for robust RAG map.

title: LaRA: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Long-Context LLMs – No Silver Bullet for LC or RAG Routing
authors:
Kuan Li, Liwen Zhang, Yong Jiang, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang, Shuai Wang, Minhao Cheng;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:36846-36867
notes: LaRA is an ICML 2025 benchmark with 2326 cases comparing RAG vs long-context LLMs across four QA tasks and three context types. Directly informs RAG vs LC routing/selection (calibration_control) and analyzes how retrieval characteristics, model strength, and context length affect RAG robustness. Strong fit for robust RAG evaluation evidence.

title: LongRAG: A Dual-Perspective Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigm for Long-Context Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: LongRAG targets long-context QA where chunking disrupts global info and retrieval noise hinders factual detail identification. Proposes information extractor and CoT-guided filter to handle noisy/distracting retrieved chunks, directly relevant to robust RAG against noisy retrieval and lost-in-the-middle distraction.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
notes: Foundational TACL 2024 paper documenting the U-shaped position bias in long-context LLMs, with explicit multi-document QA and retriever-reader case study on NQ-Open. Directly relevant to RAG context utilization/distraction; introduces evaluation protocols showing performance degrades with middle-positioned relevant info and saturates well before retriever recall. Core evidence for distraction/long-context degradation in robust RAG.

title: MMed-RAG: Versatile Multimodal RAG System for Medical Vision Language Models
authors: Peng Xia; Kangyu Zhu; Haoran Li; Tianze Wang; Weijia Shi; Sheng Wang; Linjun Zhang; James Zou; Huaxiu Yao
notes: ICLR 2025 paper on a versatile multimodal medical RAG system. Addresses robustness via domain-aware retrieval, adaptive context selection (filtering low-quality retrieved info), and preference fine-tuning to avoid interference from irrelevant retrieved content and reduce hallucinations. Fits multimodal_agentic_code as primary with secondary noisy_retrieval and calibration_control angles.

title: Measuring and Enhancing Trustworthiness of LLMs in RAG through Grounded Attributions and Learning to Refuse
authors: Maojia Song; Shang Hong Sim; Rishabh Bhardwaj; Hai Leong Chieu; Navonil Majumder; Soujanya Poria
notes: ICLR 2025 paper introduces TRUST-SCORE metric and TRUST-ALIGN alignment for LLM groundedness in RAG, covering refusal calibration, citation faithfulness, and answerability. Directly relevant to robust RAG control/calibration and evaluation.

title: Model Internals-based Answer Attribution for Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: MIRAGE uses model internals for faithful answer attribution in RAG, addressing trustworthiness/faithfulness of context usage. Relevant to robust RAG via contextual faithfulness verification; published at EMNLP 2024.

title: MuRAG: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generator for Open Question Answering over Images and Text
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: MuRAG is a foundational multimodal RAG method paper extending retrieval-augmented generation to images and text. While it evaluates under distractor settings, it does not analyze robustness, conflicts, attacks, or calibration. Background only for multimodal RAG positioning.

title: PoisonedEye: Knowledge Poisoning Attack on Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Vision-Language Models
authors:
Chenyang Zhang, Xiaoyu Zhang, Jian Lou, Kai Wu, Zilong Wang, Xiaofeng Chen;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:76811-76830
notes: ICML 2025 paper introducing PoisonedEye, the first knowledge poisoning attack against Vision-Language RAG (VLRAG) systems. Injects a single poison image-text pair into the multimodal knowledge database to manipulate LVLM responses. Clearly an adversarial corruption attack on RAG with multimodal/agentic setting as secondary.

title: Provence: efficient and robust context pruning for retrieval-augmented generation
authors: Nadezhda Chirkova; Thibault Formal; Vassilina Nikoulina; Stéphane CLINCHANT
notes: ICLR 2025 paper on context pruning for RAG that explicitly targets robustness to irrelevant retrieved context, variable amounts of relevant info, and varying context lengths across domains. Directly mitigates noisy retrieval and distractor passages by dynamically pruning sentences before generation; also unifies pruning with reranking. Clear fit for robust RAG map.

title: RAG-DDR: Optimizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Differentiable Data Rewards
authors: Xinze Li; Sen Mei; Zhenghao Liu; Yukun Yan; Shuo Wang; Shi Yu; Zheni Zeng; Hao Chen; Ge Yu; Zhiyuan Liu; Maosong Sun; Chenyan Xiong
notes: ICLR 2025 paper proposes DDR, end-to-end DPO-based training of RAG modules to align data preferences, explicitly aimed at mitigating knowledge conflict between parametric memory and retrieved evidence and shown to generalize under added noisy documents. Robustness-relevant intervention on both knowledge refinement and generation modules.

title: RAG-QA Arena: Evaluating Domain Robustness for Long-form Retrieval Augmented Question Answering
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: EMNLP 2024 paper introducing LFRQA dataset (26K queries, 7 domains) and RAG-QA Arena framework for evaluating cross-domain/OOD robustness of long-form RAG-QA systems. Directly a robust RAG evaluation benchmark with domain shift as the robustness axis.

title: RAGAs: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 18th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: System Demonstrations
notes: RAGAs introduces a reference-free automated evaluation framework for RAG with metrics for faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance. Directly addresses RAG evaluation including hallucination/faithfulness detection and retrieval quality assessment. Widely adopted benchmark/metric framework, published at EACL System Demonstrations.

title: RAGGED: Towards Informed Design of Scalable and Stable RAG Systems
authors:
Jennifer Hsia, Afreen Shaikh, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Graham Neubig;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:24139-24155
notes: RAGGED is an ICML 2025 framework systematically evaluating RAG stability/scalability across retriever-reader configurations and retrieval depths, with new metrics (RSS, RSC) and explicit focus on reader robustness to noisy/distracting retrieved contexts. Core evidence for robust RAG evaluation.

title: RAGraph: A General Retrieval-Augmented Graph Learning Framework
authors: Xinke Jiang; Rihong Qiu; Yongxin Xu; WentaoZhang; Yichen Zhu; Ruizhe zhang; Yuchen Fang; Xu Chu; Junfeng Zhao; Yasha Wang
notes: RAGraph applies retrieval-augmented concepts to Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for generalization on unseen graph data (node classification, link prediction, graph classification). It is not about robust RAG for LLM systems, does not address retrieval/context robustness of LLM-based RAG, and contains no attack/defense, calibration, or RAG-specific evaluation benchmark. Out of scope for the robust RAG map.

title: RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: Proposes RE-RAG that adds a relevance estimator to provide confidence scores, enabling decoding strategies to abstain (unanswerable) or fall back to parametric knowledge when retrieved contexts are irrelevant. Directly addresses noisy/irrelevant retrieval, calibration, and answerability in RAG.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Context Compression and Selective Augmentation
authors: Fangyuan Xu; Weijia Shi; Eunsol Choi
notes: RECOMP compresses retrieved docs into summaries and supports selective augmentation (empty summary when irrelevant), mitigating distraction and noisy retrieval in RAG. Directly relevant to robust RAG via context utilization and adaptive use of retrieval.

title: RankRAG: Unifying Context Ranking with Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs
authors: Yue Yu; Wei Ping; Zihan Liu; Boxin Wang; Jiaxuan You; Chao Zhang; Mohammad Shoeybi; Bryan Catanzaro
notes: RankRAG instruction-tunes a single LLM for both context ranking and answer generation, motivated by the trade-off that larger top-k introduces irrelevant or noisy context. Directly addresses retrieval noise/distraction via reranking and filtering. NeurIPS 2024 venue makes it useful supporting evidence for robust RAG via context selection.

title: ReDeEP: Detecting Hallucination in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Mechanistic Interpretability
authors: ZhongXiang Sun; Xiaoxue Zang; Kai Zheng; Jun Xu; Xiao Zhang; Weijie Yu; Yang Song; Han Li
notes: ICLR 2025 paper proposing ReDeEP for detecting RAG hallucinations via mechanistic interpretability (decoupling parametric vs external knowledge contributions) and AARF for mitigation. Directly addresses faithfulness/knowledge-conflict robustness in RAG; core evidence.

title: ReEval: Automatic Hallucination Evaluation for Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models via Transferable Adversarial Attacks
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2024
notes: ReEval introduces an automatic adversarial evaluation framework that perturbs retrieved evidence (answer swapping, context enriching) to test hallucination/faithfulness of retrieval-augmented LLMs. Directly relevant to robust RAG evaluation with knowledge conflict and adversarial perturbation angles.

title: Reliable Decision‑Making via Calibration‑Oriented Retrieval‑Augmented Generation
authors: Chaeyun Jang; Deukhwan Cho; Seanie Lee; Hyungi Lee; Juho Lee
notes: CalibRAG explicitly tackles RAG calibration: forecasting function predicts decision correctness from retrieved documents, addressing overconfidence under noisy/irrelevant retrieval. NeurIPS 2025 venue, directly relevant to robust RAG calibration/control.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs? A Comprehensive Study and Hybrid Approach
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: Industry Track
notes: EMNLP 2024 industry track paper that benchmarks RAG vs long-context LLMs across 9 datasets and proposes Self-Route, a self-reflection-based routing mechanism that decides when to use RAG vs LC. Relevant to robust RAG via adaptive control/selective retrieval and comparative benchmarking; analyzes RAG failure patterns and cost-performance trade-offs.

title: Retrieval Augmented Visual Question Answering with Outside Knowledge
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: Multimodal RAG method paper for OK-VQA proposing joint training of DPR retriever and answer generator. Discusses how irrelevant documents mislead training, but primary focus is on a foundational multimodal RAG architecture, not robustness analysis, attacks, conflicts, or calibration. No explicit robust-RAG angle.

title: Retrieval is Not Enough: Enhancing RAG through Test-Time Critique and Optimization
authors: Jiaqi Wei; Hao Zhou; Xiang Zhang; Di Zhang; Zijie Qiu; Noah Wei; Jinzhe Li; Wanli Ouyang; Siqi Sun
notes: AlignRAG addresses reasoning misalignment between LLM output and retrieved evidence via test-time critique; tests robustness under noisy retrieval. Core robust RAG contribution at NeurIPS 2025.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Patrick Lewis; Ethan Perez; Aleksandara Piktus; Fabio Petroni; Vladimir Karpukhin; Naman Goyal; Heinrich Küttler; Mike Lewis; Wen-tau Yih; Tim Rocktäschel; Sebastian Riedel; Douwe Kiela
notes: Foundational RAG paper by Lewis et al. (NeurIPS 2020) introducing RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token. It defines the RAG architecture and evaluates on knowledge-intensive NLP tasks but does not directly study robustness, noise, adversarial corruption, conflict, or calibration. Serves only as background/positioning for the robust RAG map, not as evidence for any specific robustness claim.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Perception: High-resolution Image Perception Meets Visual RAG
authors:
Wenbin Wang, Yongcheng Jing, Liang Ding, Yingjie Wang, Li Shen, Yong Luo, Bo Du, Dacheng Tao;
    Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267:63290-63307
notes: Visual RAG applied to high-resolution image perception in MLLMs with adaptive crop selection. Uses RAG mechanics but does not study robustness of RAG (no noise, distraction, conflict, attacks, or answerability analysis). Boundary multimodal RAG application, not robust RAG evidence.

title: Retrieving, Rethinking and Revising: The Chain-of-Verification Can Improve Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: CoV-RAG adds a verification module that scores references and answers, judges correctness, and triggers query revision and re-retrieval to mitigate external retrieval errors and internal hallucinations. Relevant as calibrated adaptive retrieval/control for robust RAG.

title: SEER: Self-Aligned Evidence Extraction for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: SEER proposes a self-aligned evidence extractor that filters distracting content from retrieved passages in RAG, improving faithfulness, helpfulness, and conciseness. Directly relevant to robust RAG via context filtering against distraction and noisy retrieval. EMNLP 2024 venue.

title: SePer: Measure Retrieval Utility Through The Lens Of Semantic Perplexity Reduction
authors: Lu Dai; Yijie Xu; Jinhui Ye; Hao Liu; Hui Xiong
notes: ICLR 2025 paper introducing SePer, a semantic-perplexity metric to quantify retrieval utility via LLM belief distribution shift. Relevant to robust RAG evaluation as it provides fine-grained measurement of when retrieval helps or hurts.

title: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
notes: EMNLP 2024 empirical study of RAG workflow components (query classification, retrieval, reranking, repacking, summarization). Not focused on adversarial robustness, but provides systematic evaluation framework and identifies practices for filtering irrelevant context (reranking, summarization), which is relevant background for robust RAG pipeline design.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
authors: Akari Asai; Zeqiu Wu; Yizhong Wang; Avirup Sil; Hannaneh Hajishirzi
notes: Self-RAG trains an LM to adaptively decide when to retrieve via reflection tokens and to self-critique relevance (IsRel) and support (IsSup) of retrieved passages. Directly addresses calibrated/adaptive retrieval, faithfulness to evidence, and robustness to irrelevant context—core foundational work for robust RAG at ICLR 2024.

title: Simple is Effective: The Roles of Graphs and Large Language Models in Knowledge-Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Mufei Li; Siqi Miao; Pan Li
notes: SubgraphRAG is a KG-based RAG method focused on efficient subgraph retrieval and reasoning over WebQSP and CWQ. While it briefly mentions reducing hallucination and pruning irrelevant info, the core contribution is retrieval efficiency/accuracy, not robustness analysis under noise, distractors, conflicts, or adversarial conditions. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: SmartRAG: Jointly Learn RAG-Related Tasks From the Environment Feedback
authors: Jingsheng Gao; Linxu Li; Ke Ji; Weiyuan Li; Yixin Lian; yuzhuo fu; Bin Dai
notes: SmartRAG jointly trains a policy network via RL to decide when to retrieve, rewrite queries, and generate answers, directly addressing adaptive retrieval and calibrated decision-making in RAG.

title: Speculative RAG: Enhancing Retrieval Augmented Generation through Drafting
authors: Zilong Wang; Zifeng Wang; Long Le; Steven Zheng; Swaroop Mishra; Vincent Perot; Yuwei Zhang; Anush Mattapalli; Ankur Taly; Jingbo Shang; Chen-Yu Lee; Tomas Pfister
notes: Speculative RAG proposes a drafter-verifier framework to improve RAG accuracy and latency. It addresses long-context position bias (lost-in-the-middle) as a side benefit, but the primary contribution is efficiency/accuracy via drafting, not a robustness mechanism against retrieval noise, distraction, conflict, or attacks. Treated as background/boundary rather than core robust RAG evidence.

title: StructRAG: Boosting Knowledge Intensive Reasoning of LLMs via Inference-time Hybrid Information Structurization
authors: Zhuoqun Li; Xuanang Chen; Haiyang Yu; Hongyu Lin; Yaojie Lu; Qiaoyu Tang; Fei Huang; Xianpei Han; Le Sun; Yongbin Li
notes: StructRAG proposes inference-time hybrid information structurization to handle scattered knowledge in knowledge-intensive reasoning. While it addresses noisy/scattered retrieval as motivation, it is primarily a RAG performance enhancement method, not an explicit robustness study (no adversarial, conflict, calibration, or systematic noise analysis). Background relevance only.

title: TRACE the Evidence: Constructing Knowledge-Grounded Reasoning Chains for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: TRACE explicitly addresses retrieval noise from imperfect retrievers in multi-hop RAG by transforming retrieved documents into a KG and constructing reasoning chains as condensed evidence. Directly tackles noisy_retrieval and lost-in-the-middle distraction. Findings of EMNLP 2024.

title: TableRAG: Million-Token Table Understanding with Language Models
authors: Si-An Chen; Lesly Miculicich; Julian Martin Eisenschlos; Zifeng Wang; Zilong Wang; Yanfei Chen; Yasuhisa Fujii; Hsuan-Tien Lin; Chen-Yu Lee; Tomas Pfister
notes: TableRAG proposes a RAG framework for large-scale table understanding using schema and cell retrieval to mitigate context length limits and lost-in-the-middle issues. While it touches on long-context distraction as motivation, the focus is on efficiency and accuracy for tabular QA rather than studying robustness to noisy/adversarial retrieval. Background only for robust RAG map.

title: The Good and The Bad: Exploring Privacy Issues in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024
notes: ACL Findings 2024 paper demonstrating privacy extraction attacks on RAG retrieval datasets via composite structured prompting. Fits adversarial_corruption (prompt-based extraction attack on RAG context/database). Relevant as attack-side evidence for robust RAG, though focus is privacy leakage rather than answer integrity.

title: Think-on-Graph 2.0: Deep and Faithful Large Language Model Reasoning with Knowledge-guided Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Shengjie Ma; Chengjin Xu; Xuhui Jiang; Muzhi Li; Huaren Qu; Cehao Yang; Jiaxin Mao; Jian Guo
notes: ToG-2 is a hybrid KG+text RAG framework aimed at improving multi-hop reasoning performance on knowledge-intensive QA. It does not explicitly study robustness aspects such as noisy retrieval, distraction, conflict, attacks, calibration, or answerability. Out of scope for robust RAG map.

title: Training Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering through Backtracking Correction
authors: Huawen Feng; ZekunYao; Junhao Zheng; Qianli Ma
notes: ICLR 2025 paper explicitly targets noise robustness in RAG via Backtracking Correction training, enabling LLMs to discern relevant vs irrelevant retrieved documents through stepwise decision-making. Directly addresses core noisy_retrieval issue with a generator-side mitigation; also touches calibration (when to use which document) and distraction handling.

title: Trustworthy Alignment of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
authors:
Zongmeng Zhang, Yufeng Shi, Jinhua Zhu, Wengang Zhou, Xiang Qi, Peng Zhang, Houqiang Li;
    Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235:59827-59850
notes: ICML 2024 paper proposing Trustworthy-Alignment, an RL-based method to align retrieval-augmented LLMs to rely on contextual (retrieved) knowledge over conflicting parametric knowledge. Directly addresses knowledge conflict in RAG, a core robustness issue. Includes theoretical and empirical analysis of model tendency under conflict.

title: Understanding Parametric and Contextual Knowledge Reconciliation within Large Language Models
authors: Jun Zhao; Yongzhuo Yang; Xiang Hu; Jingqi Tong; Yi Lu; Wei Wu; Tao Gui; Qi Zhang; Xuanjing Huang
notes: NeurIPS 2025 paper proposing entity-aware probing to mechanistically analyze how LLMs reconcile conflicting parametric vs. contextual (retrieved) knowledge in RAG. Directly studies knowledge conflict internal mechanisms, including attention competition and MLP arbitration hypotheses. Core evidence for knowledge_conflict category in robust RAG.

title: Unified Active Retrieval for Retrieval Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
notes: UAR proposes a unified adaptive/active retrieval framework that decides when to retrieve based on four orthogonal criteria (intent, knowledge, time, self-awareness). Core calibration/control problem in robust RAG: avoiding unnecessary or harmful retrieval. Also introduces AR-Bench evaluation benchmark. Published at EMNLP Findings 2024.

title: Unsupervised Information Refinement Training of Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source_or_venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
notes: INFO-RAG is an unsupervised training method that explicitly targets RAG robustness across three scenarios: complex correct texts (extraction), incomplete/incorrect texts (parametric reconciliation), and irrelevant texts. Directly addresses noisy retrieval, knowledge conflict, and distraction. ACL 2024 long paper, claims robustness gains.

title: VRAG-RL: Empower Vision-Perception-Based RAG for Visually Rich Information Understanding via Iterative Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning
authors: Qiuchen Wang; Ruixue Ding; Yu Zeng; Zehui Chen; Lin Chen; Shihang Wang; Pengjun Xie; Fei Huang; Feng Zhao
notes: VRAG-RL is a multimodal RAG method paper using RL to improve visual reasoning and retrieval through iterative tool use. It mentions irrelevant retrieval adding noise as motivation, but the core contribution is a performance-oriented RL framework with visual perception actions, not a robustness analysis, attack/defense, calibration, or benchmark for robust RAG. Out of scope for the robust RAG map.

title: xRAG: Extreme Context Compression for Retrieval-augmented Generation with One Token
authors: Xin Cheng; Xun Wang; Xingxing Zhang; Tao Ge; Si-Qing Chen; Furu Wei; Huishuai Zhang; Dongyan Zhao
notes: xRAG is an efficiency/context-compression method for RAG that compresses retrieved documents into a single embedding token via modality fusion. It targets inference cost and context length, not robustness to noisy retrieval, distractors, knowledge conflicts, adversarial attacks, or calibration. No robust RAG angle.
